Gedor
GEE-dor
proper noun
Hebrew Gedor, “a wall” or “fortified place,” a town in the hill country of Judah.

Biblical Definition

Gedor was a town in the mountainous part of the inheritance of Judah, named in the roll of the hill-country cities of their allotment: “Maarath, and Bethanoth, and Eltekon; six cities with their villages: Halhul, Bethzur, and Gedor” (Jos 15:58). Its name, “a wall” or “fortified place,” speaks of a walled town set upon the heights of Judah, between Hebron and Bethlehem. The Chronicler records that the families of Simeon, seeking pasture for their flocks, went to the entrance of Gedor, “unto the east side of the valley, to seek pasture for their flocks. And they found fat pasture and good, and the land was wide, and quiet, and peaceable” (1Ch 4:39–40); there they smote the inhabitants and dwelt in their rooms, finding rest for their flocks in the good land. Thus Gedor and its valley appear as a place of fat pasture and quietness in the hill country, a token of the goodness of the inheritance the LORD gave His people. The Scripture records little else of the town beyond its name and its place among the cities of Judah, yet its very inclusion in the inspired lists bears witness to the exactness of God’s gift. Gedor stands as a quiet monument that the LORD divided the land down to its least towns, planting His people in a country of walled cities and fat pastures, and performing to the seed of Abraham all that He had sworn to the fathers.

Webster 1828 Definition

A walled town in the hill country of Judah, near whose valley the Simeonites found fat and quiet pasture.

expand to see more

GEDOR, a town in the hill country of Judah (Jos 15:58).

It lay among the highland cities between Hebron and Bethlehem.

Its name signifies “a wall” or “fortified place.”

The Simeonites found fat pasture at its valley (1Ch 4:39–40).

It was one of the towns given into Judah’s hand.

Key Scripture

Jos 15:58 — "Halhul, Bethzur, and Gedor,"

1Ch 4:39 — "And they went to the entrance of Gedor, even unto the east side of the valley, to seek pasture for their flocks."

1Ch 4:40 — "And they found fat pasture and good, and the land was wide, and quiet, and peaceable; for they of Ham had dwelt there of old."

Jos 15:48 — "And in the mountains, Shamir, and Jattir, and Socoh,"

Modern Corruption

A place of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses to God’s faithfulness in giving His people a land of walled cities and fat pastures.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is God’s faithfulness in giving the land tribe by tribe, down to its walled hill towns and quiet valleys. Gedor was a fortified town of the Judahite highlands, and at the entrance of its valley the Simeonites found fat pasture and good, a land wide and quiet and peaceable. The LORD who divided the inheritance gave His people a good country of cities and pastures, performing to the seed of Abraham all that He had sworn to the fathers.

The naming of Gedor also stands against the skepticism that would dissolve the conquest into legend, for the careful record of its place in Judah’s allotment and the Simeonites’ resting at its valley is the precision of true history, not of myth. And the fat and quiet pasture the Simeonites found pictures the rest the LORD gives His people in the inheritance He prepares. As the flocks of Simeon found a land wide and peaceable at Gedor, so the saints find rest for their souls in the good land of promise secured for them by the greater Joshua, the Lord Jesus Christ.

Hebrew Roots

The name means “a wall” or “fortified place,” borne by a walled town of the Judahite hills.

Gedor — Hebrew Gedor, “a wall” or “fortified place.”

It lay in the hill country of Judah.

It stood among Halhul and Bethzur.

The Simeonites found fat pasture at its valley.

Its naming testifies to the exactness of God’s gift.

Usage

"Like Gedor, the walled hill towns witness that God gave His people a good land of cities and pastures."

"Gedor teaches that the LORD divided the inheritance down to its least towns, keeping all His covenant word."

"The fat and quiet pasture at Gedor pictures the rest the saints find in the inheritance secured by Christ."
